predicate_rule: Group exact-scope observations by exact period. Distinct persistence periods may not overlap. Examine the latest required periods without discarding incomplete recent evidence. Each selected period must meet declared floors for distinct source identifiers, distinct artifact hashes and coverage. Opposing threshold results in an eligible period are conflicted. Evidence older than maximum_age_days is stale. The predicate is true only when every one of the latest persistence periods passes; otherwise it is false. Missing or incomplete requirements are unknown.
time_rule: A definition is eligible only at or after its immutable effective_from time. An observation period and recording time cannot predate that definition. Evaluation time is caller supplied, marked untrusted and included in the evaluation receipt.
identity_rule: A condition identity binds typed who, verb, object, standard and polarity fields. Definition revision may change executable measurement semantics but cannot change that claim identity or scope. Scope partitions must be exhaustive and disjoint along exactly one axis.
evidence_lifecycle_rule: Only observations in the active state of the separately validated evidence-event fold may enter evaluation. Challenged, superseded, withdrawn and expired observations remain visible in history but are excluded. A correction preserves the exact source-period cell and introduces a new content-addressed observation.
all_rule: False is decisive. All true is true. One repeated non-decisive state is preserved. Mixed non-decisive states are unknown.
any_rule: True is decisive. All false is false. One repeated non-decisive state is preserved. Mixed non-decisive states are unknown.
not_rule: Invert true and false. Preserve unknown, stale and conflicted.
receipt_rule: The result binds the exact evaluator, condition definition, sorted input observation hashes, caller-supplied evaluation time, diagnostics and computed state in a content-addressed receipt.
authority_rule: Evaluation has no authority effect and cannot approve publication or authorise action.
